section.title: What the Obelisk Was For
section.form_description: One enthusiasm followed all the way down. The narrator opens on a subject they love and know cold — how a mass relay actually throws a ship, the grammar of their homeworld's oldest language, the breeding lines behind a varren pit — and talks it out well past where a listener would have stopped them, then follows a seam into the next subject and the next. An infodump, but a personal one: every fact is here because the narrator went and got it, and why they cared runs under the telling — the childhood that started it, the person who taught them, the love and the plain curiosity of it. Sections are subjects, each opening where the last one's tangent left off.
section.form_note: Rewritten after feedback. The brief is one enthusiasm talked out at length, which is tunnel; but the spine is topical and associative, not Shepard's playthrough. The order is a chain of thoughts, each section opening from an object, a feeling or an aside in the one before (a dated fragment -> the ruins the Protheans themselves dug up -> the empire -> the neighbours nobody excavated -> a goddess who was a guise -> what other species made of them -> the Mars cache -> a message meant for someone else's mind -> her own dig -> the fall and the shelters -> the Crucible -> the cycles before -> the arithmetic of a cycle -> what to leave). Nothing runs in game order; Shepard's encounters (Eden Prime beacon, Therum, Feros, Ilos, Thessia, Javik, the Leviathan trail) appear as evidence or anecdote inside a topical section, and where Liara was not there (Eden Prime beacon, the Leviathan trail; Feros and the Presidium hanar dispute she did attend, per Thomas) she draws on Shepard and on her own Shadow Broker network (she is the Broker), saying which source she is using, not merely asking Shepard. Canon kept: Shepard was marked by the beacon, Javik came aboard, the Leviathan DLC and Thessia as recorded; Legion/Tali branches and the ending are not touched, and the talk stops short of the final choice. Pre-Prothean material comes only from corpus pages (Inusannon, thoi'han/Eingana, the Leviathan of Dis, the Leviathans, the Crucible design history) and is hedged in her voice: the corpus dates the Inusannon at 127,000 years and the Protheans at 68,000-48,000 BCE, which does not fit a tidy fifty-thousand-year cycle, and she should worry at that rather than resolve it. target_words is pinned at 9000 (a one-hour spoken lecture at roughly 150 words a minute, pauses included).

required_facts.fact: The Crucible was an ancient, enormously complex superweapon designed to stop the Reapers. Its blueprint was refined by countless species across millions of years and many extinction cycles, passed secretly from one cycle to the next; no species ever managed to deploy it. The Protheans were the most recent builders, but infighting between a faction that wanted to destroy the Reapers and an indoctrinated faction that wanted to control them stopped them, and the schematics were hidden in a Prothean archive on Mars for 50,000 years. In 2186, after Liara T'Soni recovered encryption keys from a Prothean shrine on Kahje, she traveled to the Mars Archives (the mission Priority: Mars) and recognized the significance of the schematics. The Illusive Man also wanted them and sent the Cerberus infiltration unit Dr. Eva Core to steal the data and wipe the archives. After a chase and firefight, James Vega rammed Eva's shuttle with a truck and Shepard disabled her with the plans intact, though Shepard's Virmire survivor squadmate (Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko, per `virmire_survivor` / `virmire_survivor_rejoins`) was gravely injured and evacuated to Huerta Memorial Hospital on the Citadel. Eva's synthetic body was salvaged and later used to give EDI a mobile platform. The schematics were handed to the Systems Alliance, and after the fall of Earth Admiral Hackett authorized a massive galaxy-wide construction effort, with shipyards across many species building sections of the device. Scientists determined the Crucible exploited mass relay technology but could not fully explain how it worked, and that it required a final component, the Catalyst. The Prothean VI Vendetta on Thessia revealed the Catalyst was the Citadel itself, which could massively amplify the Crucible's output. The Illusive Man fled to the Citadel and alerted the Reapers, who seized the station and moved it into orbit around Earth. Hackett committed the combined fleets to Sol, and the completed Crucible was brought in behind a token defense force to dock with the Citadel, setting up the war's final choice (per `final_choice`).

During the Reaper War, with the Crucible under construction, Commander Shepard recovered two Prothean artifacts from the contested Hades Nexus cluster and turned them over to Alliance researchers on the Citadel. Both fetch missions became available after Priority: The Citadel II, but the Hades Nexus itself could only be entered after Priority: Rannoch and the resolution of the geth-quarian war, by which point it was hostile territory. In the first case, a researcher sitting in the Presidium Commons Courtyard, near the Meridian Place billboard and General Septimus Oraka's bench, needed the Obelisk of Karza for the Crucible project; his dig team had run out of time and the artifact now lay in off-limits territory. Shepard scanned the moon Kopis in the Hoplos system to recover it. The obelisk contained Prothean language translations and was likened to a Rosetta Stone for deciphering Prothean writing. In the second case, a refugee begging a turian guard for food in Bay E28 of the Docks Holding Area traded the location of Prothean ruins on Gei Hinnom in the Sheol system. Shepard scanned Gei Hinnom to recover a Prothean sphere and authorized the refugee to sell it to the Alliance; he used the money to buy food for his family and for others stranded on the Citadel. Either artifact could also turn up during a routine Search and Rescue scan, logging initially as a Citadel assignment. Delivering each artifact granted reputation, 15,000 credits, and an upgrade to the Alliance Engineering Corps war asset feeding the Crucible effort.

Project Firewalker: Prothean Site was the last of the Firewalker assignments Commander Shepard ran for Cerberus while hunting the Collectors, following Project Firewalker: Volcano Station. Data recovered at Karumto pointed Cerberus to Dr. Cayce's final known location: the moon Kopis, orbiting Makhaira in the Hoplos system of the Hades Nexus, where he had set out to excavate a Prothean site. Orbital scans showed Prothean artifacts shielded behind a powerful kinetic energy barrier and hidden automated defences. Shepard's team deployed in the Hammerhead infantry fighting vehicle. Because the barrier over the dig site could not be breached by weapons fire, the squad followed the power lines and destroyed the generators feeding it while dodging Rocket Drones; four eezo deposits could be gathered outside the base along the way. With the last generator down the barrier collapsed and the team advanced into the ruins on foot, past the bodies of the Blue Suns mercenaries Cayce's expedition had hired as guards. Logs and datapads recovered at the site told the expedition's end. Dr. Robert O'Loy had been indoctrinated by the Reapers and was leaking the team's movements to a geth ship, and had cut a deal with the Collectors - trading the Prothean find for the safety of the colony where his wife Helen lived. Dr. Cayce discovered O'Loy transmitting the data, killed him to prevent "another Eden Prime," then found the Reapers "still in my head" and resolved to destroy both the relic and himself. Shepard hacked the console and examined the artifact, similar to the one found on Eletania: it glowed green and shrank to a portable size, later displayed on the coffee table in Shepard's cabin aboard the Normandy. A follow-up message from Project Firewalker reported that an energy burst during the retrieval carried coded data that advanced Cerberus research into energy transfer and biotics, and that the artifact itself was inert and harmless.

evidence.text: It is unknown who initially began the development of the Crucible. Countless different species obtained and made contributions to the design over the course of millions of years, but none successfully deployed it before being wiped out by the Reapers. The Reapers were led to believe all traces of the design were eradicated but throughout the countless cycles, the Crucible design was continuously preserved. The latest species to try, the Protheans, were able to construct the Crucible, but before they could deploy it, infighting broke out between those who wanted to use it to destroy the Reapers and a faction that believed they could use it to control the Reapers; these separatists were later discovered to be indoctrinated. While the Protheans never had the chance to activate the Crucible, its schematics survived in a Prothean archive on Mars for the next 50,000 years.

evidence.text:
The Crucible was an ancient, highly complex superweapon device intended to stop the Reapers. Its design was contributed to by countless species across millions of years and many extinction cycles, but no species deployed it before being wiped out. The Reapers believed all traces of the design were destroyed, yet the schematics were continuously preserved and passed between cycles. The Protheans were the latest species to build it, but before they could deploy it, infighting broke out between those who wanted to use it to destroy the Reapers and a faction, later found to be indoctrinated, who wanted to control them. The schematics survived in a Prothean archive on Mars for 50,000 years.

In 2186, after recovering encryption keys from a Prothean shrine on Kahje, Liara T'Soni traveled to the Mars Archive and recognized the schematics' significance. The Illusive Man also sought them and sent the infiltration unit Dr. Eva Coré to steal the data, wiping it from the archives. After a chase involving Shepard and Liara, James Vega rammed Eva's shuttle; Shepard disabled her with the plans intact, though Shepard's Virmire survivor squadmate was gravely injured. The schematics were handed to the Systems Alliance, which began a massive galaxy-wide construction effort on Admiral Hackett's authority after the fall of Earth.

Scientists determined the device exploited mass relay technology but could not fully explain its function. It required a final component, the Catalyst, revealed by the Prothean VI Vendetta to be the Citadel itself, which could massively amplify the Crucible's energy. The Illusive Man fled to the Citadel and alerted the Reapers, who seized it and moved it into orbit around Earth. Hackett committed the galaxy's combined fleets to Sol, with the Crucible entering the battle behind a token defense force.

Shepard boarded the Citadel, opened it for docking with the Crucible, and met the Catalyst, which manifested as the boy Shepard saw die during the escape from Earth. The Catalyst described the Crucible as a crude but effective, adaptive power source, and offered Shepard choices: destroy the Reapers and all synthetics (red energy); control the Reapers at the cost of Shepard's physical form (blue energy); or synthesize organic and synthetic life (green energy). Shepard could also refuse, leaving the cycle to continue. Each firing option transmitted energy through the Charon Relay and the mass relay network, damaging the relays and, in most cases, the Citadel.

evidence.text: After recovering encryption keys from a Prothean shrine on Kahje, Liara T'Soni traveled to the Mars Archive to see what she could uncover. While examining the archives in 2186, she found the Crucible's schematics and recognized their significance as a potential means to defeat the Reapers. However, the Illusive Man also sought the same thing and sent Dr. Eva Coré to retrieve it. The schematics are wiped from the archives and stolen by Eva. Following a brief chase between the doctor, Commander Shepard, and Liara, the Cerberus mole nearly escapes Mars with the data but is prevented by the timely intervention of James Vega. In the ensuing crash of Eva's escape shuttle she's revealed to be an infiltration unit, and Shepard is able to disable her with the plans intact albeit at the cost of Shepard's squadmate who survived Virmire sustaining massive injuries at the hands of the synthetic. The schematics are then handed over to the Alliance, which immediately begins construction, a massive undertaking drawing on resources throughout the galaxy. Staggering financial costs are disregarded in the common effort to create something, *anything*, that could stop the Reapers. Despite the Crucible's elegant design, modern scientists could only determine that the device exploited the technology of mass relays, and were left to speculate on how it would ultimately function. More importantly, before the device could be activated it required one final component: the Catalyst. As revealed by the Prothean VI Vendetta, the Catalyst *is* the Citadel, the central control hub of the entire mass relay network. At some point in the past, contributors to the Crucible's design realized that it required a means to massively amplify its energy in order to be effective. The Citadel possesses this capability, and so was incorporated into the schematics. Before the galaxy could combine the Crucible with the Catalyst, however, the Illusive Man flees to the Citadel and alerts the Reapers to the plan. The Reapers seize control of the Citadel and move it to the heart of their occupied territory, in orbit around Earth. With no other option, Admiral Hackett marshals the galaxy's fleets and sends them to Sol. The Crucible enters the fray with a token defense force after the initial offensive.
evidence.for_key: Crucible Design cycles Protheans schematics Mars archive

evidence.text: In reality, Athame was not a mythical goddess but a guise crafted by the Protheans. During the height of their empire, the Protheans discovered the asari and judged that they had potential as leaders for the races of the next cycle against the Reapers. They intervened in asari development by creating the myth of a goddess, Athame, who was imparting divine gifts and knowledge through her guides, Janiri and Lucen, who were actually Protheans. Among those "gifts" was the asari's natural ability to develop biotics, which was in reality the product of years of Prothean genetic research and manipulation. Long after the Protheans departed Thessia to prevent drawing the attention of the Reapers there, the asari continued to advance with the help of a Prothean beacon and archive that had been left behind. The beacon and archive were both housed in the Temple of Athame; the temple proper was built over the archive and the beacon was concealed within a statue of Athame. The existence of the beacon and archive were kept a closely guarded secret by the asari government throughout their history, even after the Citadel Council was formed and it was declared illegal to hide Prothean technology. The information the asari gleaned allowed them to maintain a technological advantage over the rest of the galaxy's races. Even when the Reapers return to the galaxy in 2186, the asari government continues hiding the existence of the beacon, fearing political repercussion. Only when Thessia itself is attacked by the Reapers does the asari government decide to reveal the existence of the beacon and archive in the hopes that the information stored within could be of use in completing the Crucible. Commander Shepard's arrival at the Temple of Athame reveals not only Athame's true nature, but that the beacon contains a Prothean VI named Vendetta, based on personality imprints of the director of the Prothean Crucible project, including knowledge of the Catalyst, the Crucible's final component.

evidence.page: The Art of the Mass Effect Trilogy/Mass Effect 3
evidence.text: After Earth, Mars was probably the second\-most\-exciting planet to design. We knew it would have human architecture, and we wanted to capture the realistic feel of a drill site on the red planet, excavating Prothean secrets of the Mars archive. We kept the base quite low to the ground to help it survive sandstorms and other harsh Martian weather, and went with a circular design that supported a large drilling shaft down the middle. The large spokes coming off the circle serve as docking stations for shuttles and rovers. The design of the interior has a clean industrial look, more like a first\-world factory than a backwater mining station. The architecture also shows how humans' decades of studying the Prothean archives influenced the design of the mine.

evidence.page: The Art of the Mass Effect Trilogy/Mass Effect 3
evidence.text:
This page transcribes the Mass Effect 3 section of the developer commentary in the 2021 edition of The Art of the Mass Effect Trilogy, credited to Casey Hudson, Derek Watts, Chris Hepler, Karin Weekes and Ryan Cormier. It is a behind-the-scenes reference documenting the concept art and design decisions for the trilogy's final game.

Character entries cover the returning love interests Ashley Williams, Kaidan Alenko and Liara T'Soni (given new Alliance colours and heavier gear), the newly introduced James Vega, Admiral Anderson in field fatigues, a re-armored Garrus Vakarian, a matured Jack, EDI's infiltration-unit body (described as the Mass Effect version of Maria from Metropolis), the Child, and Kai Leng, whose early metal-legged design stemmed from Anderson crippling him in the novel Mass Effect: Retribution. The Illusive Man section notes a scrapped plan to turn him into a Reaper creature for the final battle.

Enemy sections describe Cerberus forces (trooper, engineer, sniper, centurion, guardian, Atlas) and Reaper forces built from converted species: the banshee (asari matriarch), cannibal (batarian), brute (krogan/turian hybrid), marauder (turian), harvester, the Reaper-converted rachni, the cut "pariah/adjutant," the roughly 160-meter Reaper destroyer, and Sovereign's leaf-insect-nymph silhouette.

Environment entries cover Earth (modeled on Vancouver), Mars and the Prothean archive, Sur'Kesh, Tuchanka and its lost krogan city, Rannoch, Thessia, the Citadel, Menae, Cerberus Headquarters, and the Normandy SR-2 repainted in Alliance blue. Other sections address the Crucible (evoking a cross between the Trinity bomb and a NASA probe), weaponry and the new omni-blade, and the Extended Cut DLC's expanded endings. DLC coverage includes the Citadel DLC (CAT6, Nyreen, Maya Brooks), Leviathan, Omega and the Talons, Javik and the Protheans, and the multiplayer firebases and character kits.

evidence.text:
The Broker Terminal was a message terminal in Liara T'Soni's cabin aboard the Normandy SR-2 in Mass Effect 3. It held correspondence and intercepted communications collected through Liara's work as the Shadow Broker, covering events across the galaxy during the Reaper War. The page reproduces its contents in full.

Many entries concerned the Crucible project: Kahlee Sanders wrote to David Anderson about the breathtaking device she was helping build; Dr. Lok reported to Admiral Hackett on nervous staff reactions to rachni working on the Crucible; Mordin Solus messaged an STG colleague about the Crucible's scale and Alliance engineers slavishly following the Mars Archive plans; Dr. Cole and Dr. T'Kisha described engineering and material shortages solved by anonymous Shadow Broker deliveries of platinum and a comm server retrieved by Kasumi Goto. Kahlee Sanders also called Jack about securing an L3-X1 biotic amp for the Grissom Academy students.

Other logs included Grunt addressing new Aralahk Company recruits, Sergeant Cavanagh apologizing for firing on allied geth primes, a purchase list for Zaeed Massani, Jacob Taylor's love letter to Dr. Brynn Cole, three unsent letters from Morinth (signed Mirala) to her sisters Rila and Falere reporting Samara's death, and Alliance correspondence to Miranda Lawson thanking her for intelligence on Cerberus. Councilor Gujir was recorded authorizing seizure of Senate eezo stockpiles to evacuate a colony. A smuggler manifest in the Yungiss system led to batarian slaves being granted asylum at the Broker's request. Feron reported to the Broker on scouting the Terminus Systems with Tazzik. An extensive set of Liara's "Prothean Notes" (2171-2186) traced her academic career, her realization that the Collectors were husked Protheans, and her shifting, disillusioned view of the Protheans after meeting Javik, ending with a list of possible book titles for a work she hoped to co-write with him.

evidence.text:
Priority: Mars was the first full mission of Mass Effect 3, acquired automatically after the Reaper assault on Earth in the prologue. Admiral Hackett ordered the Normandy to the Prothean archives on Mars, where the dig site had gone silent, to recover data that might help defeat the Reapers. Shepard landed with James Vega and found Cerberus troops executing Alliance researchers; this was the first appearance of Cerberus as an enemy faction in the trilogy, introducing Assault Troopers, Centurions and Guardians. Among the dead was a researcher named Reeves.

Inside the facility Shepard reunited with Dr. Liara T'Soni, who revealed she had discovered Prothean plans for a device ("the Crucible") capable of stopping the Reapers, and that Cerberus was there to seize them. Shepard sent Vega back to the shuttle to protect the team's exit and took Liara as squadmate. The two fought through the research complex, a sabotaged cafeteria where the air had been vented, corridors, a clean room, an autoturret gauntlet and a tram station, learning that Cerberus operatives had been implanted with Reaper technology. Shepard posed as a Cerberus team to lure a tram, then fought through a large battle at the archive station.

In the archive chamber the Illusive Man appeared by hologram. The Cerberus infiltrator Dr. Eva Coré was caught stealing the Prothean data, triggering a rooftop chase. Eva reached a shuttle, but Vega crashed his shuttle into hers. Her organic disguise was destroyed, revealing a mech infiltration unit, and on the Illusive Man's order she gravely injured Kaidan Alenko or Ashley Williams before Shepard shot her down. Shepard ordered the body brought aboard the Normandy, which left Mars orbit just as the Reapers arrived. The wounded crewmate was taken to the medical bay, and Shepard ordered Joker to set course for the Citadel. Hackett confirmed Anderson's order to seek Council aid and requested the Crucible plans for Alliance analysis. Eva's body would later be reactivated by EDI.

evidence.text:
The Firewalker Pack was a downloadable content pack for Mass Effect 2, announced on February 25, 2010 and released on March 23, 2010. Its central addition was the M-44 Hammerhead, a hover tank used for planetary exploration on hostile worlds. All combat and resource gathering in the pack's content took place within the Hammerhead; although a squadmate selection screen was shown, the choice had no effect beyond incidental comments.

The pack added five assignments under the Project Firewalker banner: Rosalie Lost, Geth Incursion, Survey Sites Located, Volcano Station, and Prothean Site, several linked to galaxy-map objectives such as Artifact Collection, Recover Research Data, and Prothean Ruin. Seven locations were opened for these missions, including the Dranek system in the Krogan DMZ, Chomos in the Phoenix Massing, the Verr system in Hawking Eta, the Yakawa system in the Caleston Rift, the Hoplos system in the Hades Nexus, and the Elysta system in the Ismar Frontier (the latter available only if the Zaeed DLC was not downloaded). The pack also placed a Prothean relic as a cabin item aboard the Normandy and added a fuel depot to the Widow system.

The Firewalker Pack required download or purchase of the Cerberus Network, and was later included as part of Mass Effect Legendary Edition.

evidence.text:
The Idenna was a starship of the quarian Migrant Fleet, a thirty-year-old decommissioned batarian Hensa-class cruiser with a crew of 693 (compared to about 80 on Alliance cruisers of similar size). She commanded several scout vessels, including the Bavea and the Cyniad.

In Mass Effect: Ascension, the Idenna served as a refuge for Kahlee Sanders, Gillian Grayson, and Hendel Mitra after they came aboard the Fleet. Her captain was regarded as a maverick and visionary who wanted to use Fleet vessels to search for new homeworlds. After Cerberus attacked the Idenna, the Admiralty Board finally accepted this policy and chose the Idenna as one of the first ships to leave the Flotilla. Her crew was cut from 694 (including newest member Lemm'Shal nar Tesleya) to around 50, and she was extensively refitted with new technology to survive five years without outside contact, a mission likened to Star Trek's Enterprise.

In Mass Effect 2, the scout Cyniad crashed on Gei Hinnom in the Sheol System, Hades Nexus, killing commanding officer Lieutenant Commander Gorlat vas Idenna; varren then killed the rest of the crew except Lieutenant Forzan vas Idenna, who was rescued by Commander Shepard and the Normandy SR-2. Captain Ysin'Mal vas Idenna sent Shepard a message of thanks for aiding the search for a new quarian homeworld.

In the first edition of Mass Effect: Deception (acknowledged by BioWare as containing lore discrepancies), the Idenna was attacked by the batarian slave ship Glory of Khar'shan, which used "drive killers" to halt her and board. The Idenna's security force, including Gillian Grayson and Hendel Mitra, repelled the boarders and captured the batarian ship. Notable crew also included Seeto'Hodda nar Idenna, Feda'Gazu vas Idenna, Hilo'Jaa vas Idenna, and Lita'Orn nar Idenna.

evidence.text:
Anomalies were oddities picked up by shipboard sensors that warranted closer investigation. They were almost always optional and had little impact on main objectives, but usually yielded resources, items, or new missions and assignments.

In the first Mass Effect, maps of uncharted worlds carried little initial information, and anomalies were denoted by question marks that changed to an X once explored.

In Mass Effect 2, when a planet or moon held an anomaly, EDI reported detecting one as the Normandy SR-2 entered planetary or lunar orbit, and the player had to actively scan the body to locate the source. During scanning, the targeting reticle showed a white line pointing toward the anomaly, and a white dot appeared on the map once the reticle drew close enough. Launching a probe at that dot unlocked the associated assignment and allowed landing on the world. Anomalies generally produced radio chatter that grew clearer as the reticle approached, though the anomalies added by the Firewalker Pack were completely silent. Locations with anomalies in Mass Effect 2 included Sinmara, Taitus and Karumto in the Caleston Rift; Tarith and Helyme in the Crescent Nebula; Neith in the Eagle Nebula; Kopis and Gei Hinnom in the Hades Nexus; Alchera, site of the Normandy Crash Site, and Lorek in the Omega Nebula; 2175 Aeia in the Rosetta Nebula; and many others, tied to N7 assignments, Project Firewalker sites, and loyalty missions.

In Mass Effect 3, EDI again announced detected anomalies, which usually indicated Search and Rescue retrievables such as fuel, War Assets, or intel, though they could also mark mission waypoints. In Mass Effect: Andromeda, Suvi Anwar reported anomalies, mentioning surface anomalies on entering planet view and non-planet-bound anomalies such as asteroids or wrecked ships on entering or scanning a system; there was at most one anomaly per planet but potentially several per system, each requiring a separate scan.

evidence.text:
Project Firewalker: Prothean Site was the final Firewalker assignment, acquired after Project Firewalker: Volcano Station. From data recovered at Karumto, Cerberus located Dr. Cayce's last known position on Kopis, a moon orbiting Makhaira in the Hades Nexus, where he had set out to excavate a Prothean site. Scans showed Prothean artifacts protected by a powerful energy barrier and hidden automated defenses.

The mission began with Shepard's squad in the Hammerhead. The kinetic barrier over the dig site was too strong for weapons, so it had to be brought down by destroying the generators powering it, following the power lines while evading Rocket Drones. Four eezo deposits could be collected outside the base. Once the last generator fell, the barrier dropped and the squad continued into the ruins on foot, passing dead Blue Suns mercenaries hired to guard the site.

Logs and datapads revealed the tragedy: Dr. Robert O'Loy had been indoctrinated by the Reapers and was leaking the team's data to a geth ship, and had made a deal with the Collectors, trading the Prothean find for the safety of his wife Helen's colony. Dr. Cayce discovered O'Loy's betrayal, killed him, then found the Reapers "still in my head" and resolved to destroy the relic and himself. Shepard hacked the console and examined the relic—similar to the one on Eletania—which glowed green and shrank to a manageable size, afterward displayed on the coffee table in Shepard's cabin. A follow-up email from Project Firewalker reported that an energy burst during the retrieval contained coded data advancing research on energy transfer and biotics, and that the artifact was inert and not dangerous.

evidence.text: Rocket Drones were autonomous drones equipped with rocket launchers, used in 2185 to guard certain areas in Mass Effect 2. They attacked from a distance at varying heights and often moved to flank enemies. Most possessed only shielding and were destroyed once it was stripped, though the Rocket Drones on Kopis also had health; being unable to take cover, they compensated with high maneuverability. Shield-stripping powers and weapons such as Overload and Disruptor Ammo were effective against them, and because they were flying enemies they were immune to some biotic powers. On Kopis the Hammerhead was used to fight them, its guided missiles countering their unguided rockets. During the Lair of the Shadow Broker they were affected by Singularity (flying in circles) and instantly destroyed by Stasis. In Legion: A House Divided, Shepard could override inactive rocket drones and turn them against the geth at the Heretic Station. Drones in the Project Firewalker assignments resembled the Geth Rocket Drone from the original Mass Effect.

evidence.text:
The M-080 was a large six-wheeled infantry fighting vehicle (IFV) armed with a turret carrying two coaxial barrels, a machine gun and a main cannon. Three variants appeared: the base IFV, an APC that removed the turret for an armored passenger top, and a missile artillery version mounting two powerful Thanix missiles. Like the M29 Grizzly and M35 Mako it was non-drivable scenery, and according to The Art of Mass Effect it was actually an early design of the M35 Mako, built on a near-identical chassis.

By 2185 the M-080 was in use across many factions. In Mass Effect 2, IFV variants appeared at an Eclipse base on Daratar (painted black) and a Blue Suns base on Joab (metallic). An Eclipse M-080 sat in Donovan Hock's garage during Kasumi Goto's loyalty mission, its main gun used to blast open a wall, and an APC variant was also parked there. Another M-080 was seen crashed through a wall of the hospital on Tuchanka bearing krogan clan markings, and overturned examples littered Kopis during the Project Firewalker: Prothean Site mission.

In Mass Effect 3, Cerberus fielded APC variants at its Mars base and the Alliance used the same APCs and missile-truck variants during the final battle for Earth. Shepard used one missile truck to destroy the Reaper Destroyer guarding the London beam, firing two Thanix missiles into its "eye" after fighting off Marauders, Banshees, and Brutes. The APC also served as multiplayer map scenery on Firebase Condor and Firebase London.

evidence.text: |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- | **Vendetta** is a Prothean Virtual Intelligence. It resides within a Prothean beacon located in the Temple of Athame on Thessia. Vendetta was modeled after Pashek Vran, the overseer of the Protheans' Crucible project. It contains valuable information pertaining to the Crucible's construction and implementation. During the Reaper assault on Thessia, Vendetta is activated by Commander Shepard. After verifying that it is in a post\-Prothean cycle, Vendetta detects the presence of Reapers and attempts to shut down, declaring the cycle has already reached its "extinction terminus." Shepard urges the VI to wait, demanding to know what the Catalyst is. Vendetta explains that the Crucible is not of Prothean design, and that the Protheans' attempt to use it was sabotaged by a splinter group who argued the Reapers should be controlled rather than destroyed \-\- much like Cerberus in the present cycle. These separatists were later discovered to be indoctrinated. On further questioning, Vendetta also mentions that the Protheans have found similar patterns of evolution and dissolution occurred in every galactic cycle. Each path of advancement and conflict happened differently but in fundamentally similar ways \-\- too similar to be merely coincidences. Whether these similarities include synthetic/organic confrontation, indoctrinated splinter groups, or structure of galactic politics remains unclear. Vendetta infers that the Reapers are merely "servants" of the pattern, not its creators, but cannot identify their true master or motive, only its intention: galactic annihilation. Shepard repeats their earlier demand to know about the Catalyst. If Javik is around, Vendetta detects him as Prothean, further revealing it knew about his mission before asking if the present cycle can win. Javik argues the current cycle has earned the right to try. Vendetta deems the odds of success remote, but will try to help by assisting with the Catalyst once the Crucible is complete. However, it detects an indoctrinated presence, Kai Leng, and enters a fail\-safe mode in an ultimately futile attempt to avoid capture. Kai Leng defeats Shepard with the assistance of an A\-61 Mantis Gunship, takes the VI, and delivers it to the Illusive Man. Shepard later learns the true nature of the Catalyst from Vendetta after reaching the Illusive Man's office on Cronos Station. The Catalyst is in fact the Citadel, and it serves to enhance dark energy emissions and coordinate the entire mass relay network, thereby extending the Crucible's range. Because the Crucible cannot defeat the Reapers in its current state, the Citadel was incorporated into the design at some point many cycles ago, to use the Reapers' own technology against them. Vendetta was programmed to withhold the information for fear of the Reapers learning of the Catalyst's intended use before the Crucible was completed. Unfortunately, the Illusive Man broke through the VI's security protocols, learned its secrets anyway, and informed the Reapers of the Catalyst's true nature. They responded accordingly, seizing the Citadel and placing it in orbit of humanity's homeworld, Earth. The Reapers would protect their station at all costs and Vendetta predicts that the probability of accessing it to be remote. Shepard's still optimistic though, prompting Vendetta to wish them success. Shortly later, after Kai Leng's death, Vendetta informs Shepard the Reapers are preparing to complete the harvest of humanity. It recommends investigating a means of preserving information for the next cycle, hoping that the warnings will be heeded early enough. Shepard can interject at any point, vowing to personally stop the Reapers.

evidence.text:
Vendetta was a Prothean Virtual Intelligence residing within a Prothean beacon in the Temple of Athame on Thessia. It was modeled after Pashek Vran, the overseer of the Protheans' Crucible project, and held valuable information about the Crucible's construction and implementation. During the Reaper assault on Thessia in 2186, Commander Shepard activated Vendetta. After verifying it was in a post-Prothean cycle and detecting Reapers, it attempted to shut down, declaring the cycle had reached its "extinction terminus," but Shepard urged it to wait.

Vendetta explained that the Crucible was not of Prothean design, and that the Protheans' attempt to use it had been sabotaged by an indoctrinated splinter group who argued the Reapers should be controlled rather than destroyed, much like Cerberus. It said the Protheans had found that similar patterns of evolution and dissolution recurred in every galactic cycle, too similar to be coincidence, and inferred the Reapers were merely "servants" of that pattern, not its creators, its intention being galactic annihilation. If Javik was present, Vendetta identified him as Prothean and revealed it had known of his mission. It agreed to help with the Catalyst once the Crucible was complete, then detected the indoctrinated Kai Leng and entered a fail-safe mode; Kai Leng, aided by an A-61 Mantis Gunship, defeated Shepard, took the VI, and delivered it to the Illusive Man.

At Cronos Station, Shepard learned from Vendetta that the Catalyst was the Citadel itself, which enhanced dark energy emissions and coordinated the mass relay network to extend the Crucible's range. Vendetta had been programmed to withhold this so the Reapers would not learn of it before the Crucible was finished, but the Illusive Man broke its security and informed the Reapers, who seized the Citadel and moved it into orbit of Earth. After Kai Leng's death, Vendetta reported the Reapers were preparing to complete the harvest of humanity and recommended preserving information for the next cycle. Like the other Prothean VIs Vigil and Victory, its name began with the letter V.

evidence.text: Following the resolution of the quarian\-geth conflict, the asari councillor requests that Shepard come speak with her on the Citadel. Though the Crucible's construction nears completion, the absence of the Catalyst still makes it useless against the Reapers. The Councillor reveals to Shepard that there is a highly classified artifact located on Thessia that may help the Commander identify the Catalyst; however, she urges haste, as the Reapers have descended on Thessia in droves, seeking to annihilate the most advanced race in the galaxy. En route to Thessia, Liara, who insists on coming to help her homeworld, explains that the artifact is housed in the Temple of Athame, a deity whose worship is nearly as old as the asari, but has fallen out of practice. Arriving on Thessia to find the asari military fighting a losing battle against Reaper forces, Shepard and the squad make their way to the temple, where a science team is purported to be waiting for them. They arrive at the temple to find a security field blocking entrance, strangely high\-security for a temple of a dead religion. When Liara deactivates it, they enter the temple and find the scientists dead, but not at Reaper hands. They search the temple which houses artifacts related to Athame's worship, including ones that look suspiciously Prothean. While Liara explains the temple's history, Shepard comes to a realisation; the artifact the Councillor sent them to find is a Prothean Beacon hidden within the temple. Considering the temple's age, the beacon is likely the reason why the asari are technologically and scientifically ahead of the other races, and they have directly violated Council law by keeping the beacon to themselves. The beacon is powered up by the detection of one with Prothean\-like brain patterns (which Shepard received in the form of the Cipher) and once the squad fully activate it, a Prothean VI identifying itself as Vendetta appears. Establishing that it is in a post\-Prothean cycle and detecting nearby Reaper forces, it attempts to shut down, but Shepard insists that it wait and provide information on the Catalyst and Crucible. Vendetta explains that the Crucible is not of Prothean origin, but is a cumulative design spanning countless galactic cycles stretching back millions of years. The Protheans themselves never used it because their efforts were sabotaged by a splinter faction who (like Cerberus in the present cycle) argued the Protheans should control the Reapers, not destroy them. By the time it was discovered the separatists were indoctrinated, it was too late; the Prothean order of battle was too fractured to coordinate an effort to activate it. Vendetta also mentions that the Protheans learned that similar patterns of evolution and dissolution occur in every galactic cycle, with each path of advancement and conflict happening differently but in fundamentally similar ways \- too similar to be merely chance. Vendetta infers that the Reapers are "servants" of the pattern, not its creator, but cannot identity their true master or motive, only its intention: galactic annihilation. Before Vendetta can specify what the Catalyst is, it detects an indoctrinated presence nearby and shuts down. The intruder is revealed to be Kai Leng who demands their attention, pulling a drone from his coat and remarking that "Someone would like to talk with you". The drone projects a hologram of the Illusive Man, who has learnt of the Thessia beacon from the Mars Archive and mocks Liara for missing it. The Illusive Man goes on to expand on his belief and convince Shepard that controlling the Reapers is the best course of action and that the Thessia beacon contains the information to do so. Shepard asserts their conviction to destroying the Reapers and dismisses the Illusive Man's scheme, accusing him of being indoctrinated. Rebuffed, the Illusive Man orders Leng to kill Shepard and recover the data. A vicious battle ensues, but Leng is unable to gain the upper hand. Leng calls in assistance, ordering a Cerberus gunship to destroy the temple's structural supports and the temple begins to collapse. Shepard and squad are forced to react quickly to save themselves and by the time they recover, Leng has already acquired the data and fled aboard the gunship. They can only watch helplessly as Leng's ship escapes and more Reapers descend to complete the destruction of Thessia. After escaping to the Normandy, the asari Councillor contacts Shepard, though the Commander delays the meeting out of reluctance. The Councillor eagerly requests information on the Catalyst and when it will complete the Crucible, but Shepard is forced to tell her of Cerberus' interference and their failure to acquire the data. Realising that asari civilisation, maybe all civilisation, may now be lost, the asari Councillor cuts communication, leaving Shepard to brood on their failure.

evidence.text:
"Valhallan Threshold: Prothean Data Drives" was a fetch mission in Mass Effect 3, available after Priority: The Citadel II and only after the Cerberus attack on the Citadel. Commander Shepard could overhear an Alliance soldier talking to his superior about the Crucible near the door to the Normandy at Normandy Dock: Bay D24. The soldier knew the location of Prothean data drives that could aid the Crucible project, on the planet Garvug in the Valhallan Threshold. Alternatively, a Search and Rescue scan operation over the planet Paz in the Valhallan Threshold yielded the drives directly, in which case the journal entry was labeled "Citadel: Prothean Data Drives" and instructed Shepard to find someone on the Citadel who could use them.

The walkthrough was to scan Garvug (Paz) to obtain the artifact and return it to the soldier on the Citadel. Completion granted 5 Reputation, 15,000 credits, and an upgrade to the War Asset Alliance Engineering Corps. Trivia noted the soldier's wide speaking radius made the mission hard to avoid triggering, though it could be bypassed by rushing past him, save/reloading, or completing a Leviathan mission that deposited Shepard directly on the Normandy.

evidence.text:
The Protheans were an ancient race that vanished roughly 50,000 years ago after building a galaxy-wide empire. They were long credited with creating the Citadel and the mass relays, though in truth they only inherited that Reaper technology. Anthropoidal in form, they had two pairs of dual-pupiled eyes, three pairs of nostrils, a layered head carapace, three-fingered hands, and a flanging voice like turians. A unique trait was an experiential exchange system: by touch, a Prothean could absorb another's memories, skills, or language. They had quad-strand DNA, some resistance to low radiation, and at least some members wielded potent biotics.

After achieving spaceflight, the Protheans discovered ruins of the earlier inusannon and learned mass effect physics, gaining a centuries-long secret advantage. Facing a hostile machine intelligence, they decided all organic life must unite under their rule; resisting species were conquered and assimilated, coming to call themselves "Prothean." United, they held off the machines in the Metacon War. They observed and cultivated primitive species including asari, hanar, humans, quarians, salarians and turians, intending eventually to offer them the "choice" of joining the empire.

The Reapers arrived around 48,000 BCE, entering through the Citadel, decapitating the government, disrupting the relay network, and using Citadel census data to hunt every Prothean. Their unified empire and single military doctrine became fatal weaknesses. Indoctrinated Protheans acted as sleeper agents. Subject races like the densorin and the AI zha'til were destroyed; the Protheans themselves annihilated the zha'til by sending a star supernova. Some Protheans built a Crucible from designs left by prior civilizations, but indoctrinated builders sabotaged it. After centuries the Reapers killed or enslaved every Prothean and withdrew into dark space.

Survivors persisted in stasis. On Ilos, the Conduit research team under Ksad Ishan went dark; the VI Vigil cut power to non-essential pods until only about a dozen scientists remained, who later used the Conduit to reach the Citadel and alter the keepers' signal to trap the Reapers. On Eden Prime, nearly a million warriors and their commander Javik were stored; traitors betrayed the site, most pods were destroyed, and the VI Victory kept only Javik's pod alive. Shepard could revive Javik in 2186. Meanwhile the Reapers repurposed captured Protheans into the Collectors, directed by Harbinger to abduct humans for a Human-Reaper.

The Protheans held evolution, the "Cosmic Imperative," as the universe's driving force. Their influence shaped the asari (uplifted as a possible failsafe), humans (via the Mars archive) and the hanar, who worship them as the "Enkindlers." Notable Protheans included Javik, avatar of vengeance, and the guides Janiri and Lucen of asari myth. Prothean tech included mind-to-mind beacons, memory shards, indoctrination detection, kinetic barrier grids, the Particle Rifle, the flagship Penumbra Apex, and the Conduit.
